blocks.text: PSG have been the most dominant home side in Ligue 1 so far. In four league games at the Parc des Princes they are unbeaten, with a goal difference of +8.

items: Record: W3 D1 L0 · 11 scored, 3 conceded (2.75 / 0.75 per game).
Chance creation: 9.8 xG at home (2.45 per game), the highest in the league.
The one dropped result (Monaco, 1-1) came despite a 2.1 xG performance — a finishing variance game rather than a structural concern.
Defensively, two of the three goals conceded came from fast breaks after PSG lost the ball high up the pitch.

blocks.text: Context: four matches is a small sample. Treat home splits as directional, not definitive.

blocks.text: Here are the six signals our models and analysts weighted most for PSG vs Marseille, grouped by which side they favour. None of them is decisive on its own.

items: Home control (strong · PSG): unbeaten at home, 66% average possession, opponents held to 0.75 goals per game.
Chance quality (moderate · PSG): xG difference of +9.1 vs Marseille's +3.7.
Transition threat (moderate · Marseille): league-high 3.1 counter-attack shots per game, aimed at PSG's high line.
Set pieces (moderate · Marseille): 5 set-piece goals — joint-most in Ligue 1.
Rest days (weak · Marseille): PSG played in the Champions League four days ago; OM had a full week.
Rivalry volatility (neutral): last six meetings averaged 5.2 cards; two were decided after 75'.

blocks.text: The biggest open variable is PSG's centre-back fitness test. Re-check this once the official line-ups are published (≈ 60 minutes before kick-off).

blocks.text: Both teams arrive in good form, but the shape of that form is different: PSG's comes from sustained territorial control, Marseille's from efficiency in transition.

items: PSG's only defeat came away at Bayern Munich in the Champions League — their Ligue 1 run is unbeaten.
Marseille's xG (7.9) is below their actual goals (9): they've been clinical, which tends to regress over larger samples.
Defensively the two sides are closer than the league table implies.

What makes this fixture difficult to predict?

blocks.text: Le Classique is one of the harder Ligue 1 fixtures to read, even with PSG as the stronger side on paper. Five factors widen the range of plausible outcomes:

items: Line-up uncertainty — a late fitness test at centre-back and possible midfield rotation after a midweek European away trip.
Discipline — red cards in 2 of the last 6 meetings. A sending-off invalidates most pre-match signals.
Style clash — PSG's high line is exactly what Marseille's transition game is built to exploit.
Small samples — seven league games is early-season data, and home/away splits rest on 3–4 matches.
Rivalry dynamics — historical meetings have produced late goals and momentum swings (OM led 2-0 at half-time in one recent 2-2).
